name: Vernon Bown
bio: Vernon Bown was a Lincoln Brigade veteran who guarded the Wade house after a Black family bought a home in a white Louisville neighborhood in 1954. He was charged under Kentucky sedition law and also with the bombing of the house, and was jailed under bail set at $10,000 to $20,000.
charges: Kentucky sedition / criminal syndicalism — for aiding a Black family's move into a white Louisville neighborhood; also charged with the bombing.
convicted: Indicted for sedition and charged with the bombing.

name: Larue Spiker
bio: Larue Spiker was a social worker indicted in October 1954 under Kentucky sedition law in the Louisville case over aiding a Black family's move into a white neighborhood. She was held under a $10,000 bond.
charges: Kentucky sedition / criminal syndicalism — for aiding a Black family's move into a white Louisville neighborhood.

name: Mary Louise Gilbert
bio: Mary Louise Gilbert was a social worker indicted under Kentucky sedition law in the 1954 Louisville case over aiding a Black family's move into a white neighborhood. She was held under a $10,000 bond.
charges: Kentucky sedition / criminal syndicalism — for aiding a Black family's move into a white Louisville neighborhood.

name: I. O. Ford
bio: I. O. Ford was indicted in October 1954 under Kentucky sedition law in the Louisville case over aiding a Black family's move into a white neighborhood. He was jailed because he could not raise bail.
charges: Kentucky sedition / criminal syndicalism — for aiding a Black family's move into a white Louisville neighborhood.

name: Louis Lubka
bio: Louis Lubka was a General Electric union shop steward who was fired for refusing to testify in the 1954 Louisville sedition case. He faced a second sedition indictment over aiding a Black family's move into a white neighborhood.
charges: Kentucky sedition / criminal syndicalism — for aiding a Black family's move into a white Louisville neighborhood.
convicted: Faced a second sedition indictment; fired for refusing to testify.
sentence: Lost his job; faced sedition charges.

name: Giles Cooper
bio: Giles Cooper was jailed for 30 hours for contempt in Lexington, Kentucky for refusing to testify against the Braden sedition defendants. The case arose from aiding a Black family's move into a white Louisville neighborhood.
charges: Contempt — refusing to testify against the Braden sedition defendants.

name: Andrew Wade
bio: Andrew Wade was a Black Navy veteran whose 1954 purchase of a home in a white Louisville neighborhood triggered the sedition case. He was harassed and charged with breach of peace after his house was bombed.
charges: Breach of peace / harassment charges after buying a home in a white Louisville neighborhood (his house was then bombed).
convicted: Charges after his home was bombed; he was the target, not the bomber.

name: Molka Reich Bare
bio: Molka Reich Bare was cited for contempt in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions. She was sentenced to one year and sued contesting the order.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.
sentence: One year; she sued contesting the order.

name: Maurice Carroll
bio: Maurice Carroll was a Jewish Cultural Center director cited for contempt in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for invoking the Fifth Amendment. He was convicted, but his one-year term was voided by the Florida Supreme Court in November 1954.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.
sentence: One year (voided by the Florida Supreme Court, November 1954).

name: Morris Robinsky
bio: Morris Robinsky was cited for contempt in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for invoking the Fifth Amendment. He was convicted, his one-year term was voided in November 1954, and he was later threatened with a new indictment.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.
sentence: One year (voided November 1954); later threatened with a new indictment.

name: Jose Carbonell
bio: Jose Carbonell was jailed for one year without bail in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions. The Florida Supreme Court granted him bail in July 1954.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.
sentence: One year without bail; bail granted by the Florida Supreme Court in July 1954.

name: Philip Feldman
bio: Philip Feldman was jailed in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions. He was freed on $2,500 bail.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.

name: David Lippert
bio: David Lippert was ordered before the court in July 1954 in the Dade County 'subversive activities' probe. The probe jailed and cited people for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.
convicted: Ordered before the court in July 1954.

name: Charles Marks
bio: Charles Marks was jailed and cited for contempt in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions. The probe targeted people who invoked the Fifth before the county.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.

name: Walter Marks
bio: Walter Marks, son of Charles Marks, was ordered before the court in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe. The probe jailed and cited people for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.

name: Mike Shantzek
bio: Mike Shantzek was an Abraham Lincoln Brigade veteran jailed in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions. He was released on $2,500 bail.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.

name: Max Shlafrock
bio: Max Shlafrock was cited and jailed in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions. The probe targeted people who invoked the Fifth before the county.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.

name: Charles Smolikoff
bio: Charles Smolikoff was a former Transport Workers organizer jailed without bail in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions, despite a rheumatic heart condition. The probe targeted people who invoked the Fifth before the county.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.
sentence: Jailed without bail (despite a rheumatic heart).

name: Leah Benemovsky
bio: Leah Benemovsky was cited and jailed in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions. The probe targeted people who invoked the Fifth before the county.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.

name: Augusta Birnberg
bio: Augusta Birnberg was cited for contempt in the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions. She sent her child away during the ordeal.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.
sentence: Cited for contempt; she sent her child away.

name: Emanuel Graff
bio: Mrs. Emanuel Graff was a Groveland-defense and Wallace activist subpoenaed in a maternity hospital during the 1954 Dade County 'subversive activities' probe. She was ordered before the grand jury for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer questions.
charges: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.
convicted: Subpoenaed and ordered before the grand jury.
sentence: Subpoenaed in a maternity hospital; ordered before the grand jury.

name: Leo Sheiner
bio: Leo Sheiner was a radical Miami attorney summarily disbarred after invoking the Fifth Amendment before a Senate subcommittee during the 1954 red-hunt. His disbarment came for refusing to testify.
charges: Disbarment after invoking the Fifth Amendment before a Senate subcommittee.

name: Elba Chase Nelson
bio: Elba Chase Nelson was the 1938 Communist gubernatorial candidate in New Hampshire, prosecuted under the state's 1951 anti-subversion law. She was charged for refusing to answer the attorney-general's subversion probe.
charges: Refusing to answer the New Hampshire attorney-general's subversion probe.
convicted: Prosecuted under the New Hampshire anti-subversion law.

name: Homer Chase
bio: Homer Chase was a Communist and the son of Elba Chase Nelson, prosecuted under New Hampshire's 1951 anti-subversion law. He was charged for refusing to answer the attorney-general's subversion probe.
charges: Refusing to answer the New Hampshire attorney-general's subversion probe.
convicted: Prosecuted under the New Hampshire anti-subversion law.

name: Irma Otto
bio: Irma Otto was the Progressive Party state chairman in New Hampshire, subpoenaed under the state's 1951 anti-subversion law. She answered only her name before the attorney-general's subversion probe.
charges: Refusing to answer the New Hampshire attorney-general's subversion probe.

name: Joe Stern
bio: Joe Stern was cited for contempt of the Ohio un-American activities commission in 1954. He was fined $500 and given 10 days.
charges: Contempt of the Ohio un-American activities commission.

name: Emmett Brown
bio: Emmett Brown was a Black man cited for contempt of the Ohio un-American activities commission in 1954. He was fined $500 and given 10 days.
charges: Contempt of the Ohio un-American activities commission.

name: Reuel Stanfield
bio: Reuel Stanfield was tried for contempt of the Ohio un-American activities commission in 1954. He was acquitted.
charges: Contempt of the Ohio un-American activities commission.

name: Ben Gold
bio: Ben Gold was president of the Fur & Leather Workers Union, found guilty in 1954 of falsely swearing a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit, in a case marked by alleged FBI jury tampering. He was free on $10,000 bail.
charges: False statement in a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit.
convicted: Found guilty in 1954 (alleged FBI jury tampering).

name: Melvin Hupman
bio: Melvin Hupman was a UE local leader in Cincinnati convicted in January 1954 of falsely swearing a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit. He was sentenced to five years and a $5,000 fine.
charges: False statement in a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit.

name: Anthony Valentino
bio: Anthony Valentino was a UE figure convicted of falsely swearing a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit. He was sentenced to five years and remained free on bail pending appeal.
charges: False statement in a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit.

name: Craig Vincent
bio: Craig Vincent was a Progressive Party founder and New Mexico resort operator cited for contempt at the Clinton Jencks Taft-Hartley trial for invoking the Fifth Amendment. The citation was later dismissed.
charges: Contempt at the Jencks Taft-Hartley trial (Fifth Amendment).

name: Michael Quill
bio: Michael Quill was president of the Transport Workers Union, indicted on criminal-libel counts in Brooklyn in 1954. He faced three counts of criminal libel.
charges: Criminal libel (three counts).
